subject: The repository method for preserving a scientific claim's evidence boundary
central_question: Which evidence boundaries should an article retain when explaining a study?
reader_promise: General readers will understand which research details control a claim and why limitations belong beside the result.

claims.text: The science module requires publication status, population or material, method, measured outcome, and limitations to remain identifiable.
A compact research-object record can make omitted evidence boundaries easier to inspect before drafting.
claims.qualification: This is a design rationale, not measured proof that the method improves accuracy.

claims.text: The method improves the error rate of a particular newsroom.
claims.qualification: No benchmark or newsroom evidence is supplied.

media.reason: A conceptual flow makes the evidence boundary easier to inspect.

brief.purpose: Explain the path from research object to bounded article claim.
brief.reader_benefit: Readers can inspect where method, result, and limitation enter the claim.
brief.evidence_basis: The selected science and article runtime modules.
acceptance_criteria: alt text communicates the evidence path
